item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the substantially more mergeable patch because it implements the requested convenience API with the established multipart helper and stays narrowly scoped. Both candidates incorrectly bypass FilesService.Add, but A additionally violates an explicit contract prohibition by introducing association fields and new multipart machinery.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature and uses multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required buffered, replayable multipart body.","B preserves FilesOption behavior and avoids unrelated API expansion; A adds six association options despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields.","A unnecessarily extends the shared multipart helper with Field and NewFileWithFields, duplicating machinery outside the requested scope.","Both implementations duplicate Add's request, decoding, and error logic by calling Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, so neither fully satisfies the frozen contract; this is a clear follow-up required for B before merge approval is final."],"risks_a":["Explicitly violates the contract by adding association fields and public WithFile*ID APIs.","Changes internal multipart infrastructure unnecessarily.","Upload bypasses Add and duplicates its request/response behavior, risking future semantic drift."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses Add rather than centralizing option handling and error semantics through it.","Tests do not cover source-reader error propagation.","The retry test uses bytes.NewReader rather than a streamed source such as an open file, so streamed-content retry coverage is weaker than required."]}
